claims.claim: Each gunicorn sync worker handles one request at a time; while it waits on I/O it does nothing, so at peak requests queue behind busy workers
claims.about: Python gunicorn sync workers (Django; Flask sync used as the closest measured stand-in)
claims.measured: python-flask (sync), I/O wait at 256 connections: 276 req/s, p50 915 ms, p99 932 ms, CPU 18%
claims.why: With a 10 ms wait per request, the sync server reached only 276 req/s and its p50 rose to about 915 ms, which is the queueing behind blocked workers that the claim describes.

claims.claim: Waiting workers use almost no CPU, so a CPU-based autoscaler doesn't add pods when the queue grows
claims.measured: python-flask I/O wait CPU 18% (gthread 19%), while p50 was 915 ms
claims.why: The sync and gthread servers stayed at about 18–19% CPU while requests queued for nearly a second, so CPU does not reflect the backlog.

claims.claim: Go would give each pod far more concurrent requests, which addresses the queueing
claims.measured: I/O wait: go-gin 20,235 req/s and go-nethttp 18,905 req/s vs python-flask 276 req/s
claims.why: Go handled about 70 times as many requests per second on the I/O-wait test, so 'far more' points the right way.

claims.claim: The dependency latencies stay the same in any language; a Go service would still spend that time waiting, and the external calls set the floor on latency
claims.measured: go-gin I/O wait p50 12.13 ms, go-nethttp 12.82 ms, against a 10 ms simulated upstream wait
claims.why: Go's median latency sat just above the 10 ms upstream wait, so the wait time still sets the floor.

claims.claim: gthread workers give more concurrent requests per pod than sync workers
claims.about: gunicorn gthread vs sync (Flask as stand-in)
claims.measured: I/O wait: flask-gthread 374 vs flask 276 req/s; DB single query: 2,119 vs 1,529 req/s
claims.why: gthread measured higher than sync on the I/O and database tests, though only by about 1.35x on the I/O-wait test.

claims.claim: gevent gives more concurrency than gthread for I/O-bound sync code
claims.about: gunicorn gevent vs gthread (Flask as stand-in)
claims.measured: I/O wait: flask-gevent 2,956 vs flask-gthread 374 req/s; DB single query: 1,905 vs 2,119; DB 20 queries: 369 vs 504
claims.why: On the pure I/O-wait test gevent handled about 8 times as many requests as gthread, though it measured slightly lower than gthread on the Postgres tests.

claims.claim: Go is worth extracting for a CPU-bound hot path (implied to be much faster than Python for CPU-bound work)
claims.measured: fib(20): go-gin 18,218 and go-nethttp 15,093 req/s vs python-flask 1,078 and gthread 1,149 req/s
claims.why: Go was roughly 14–17 times faster than the Flask variants on the CPU-bound test.

claims.claim: In a spike of one endpoint, Go vs Django with the same real dependencies, the difference will be smaller than the proposal assumes because the dependencies dominate
claims.why: Django is not among the measured servers, the proposal's assumed speed-up is not stated, and the benchmark has no test with 40–80 ms dependencies.
